comment: Two kinds of rules, they cannot be mixed in one rule:
'mock'                  - the proxy answers by itself, the request NEVER reaches the server;
'request' / 'response'  - the request DOES reach the server, the request and/or the real answer are changed.
A rule with 'mock' and 'request' or 'response' together is an error and is skipped.
=== 1. Mock the response ('mock'): the request never reaches the server ===

name: Status code with a JSON body (objects/arrays are serialized as JSON)
Raw string body, sent as is with a custom Content-Type
No body: a default JSON body describing the mock is returned
Match by query parameters (url is then matched without the query string)
Extra response headers and a delay before responding
Hang for N seconds, then drop the connection
Drop the connection immediately (network error in the browser)
Without automatic CORS headers (to reproduce a CORS failure)

comment: === 2. Change the request ('request'): the changed request goes to the real server ===

name: Request: change fields of the JSON body (null removes a field, nested objects are merged)
Request: replace the whole body
Request: set, change and remove query parameters
Request: headers (null removes one, e.g. log out a single request)
Request: fields of an HTML form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
Request: find and replace in any body (plain text: no special characters)
Request: several replacements, a regular expression with a group
Request: change the method
Request: send to another address (other stand, API version, local backend)
Request: hold it before sending to the server

comment: === 3. Change the real response ('response'): the server answers, the app gets a changed answer ===

name: Response: change fields of the real JSON
Response: real body, different status
Response: replace the whole body (the real headers stay)
Response: find and replace in the body
Response: headers (disable caching, add a header)
Response: slow real server

comment: === 4. Request and response together: one real call to the server, both ends changed ===

name: Expired session: drop the token, show what the app gets on 401
Order with a huge amount, and the server reply is slowed down
Disabled rule: kept in the file but ignored
